Thanks again for the walkthrough today 	6 helpful session. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can get a pilot kickstarted:

- Goals: low-latency chat for our customer-facing assistant, and embedding generation for indexing.
- Target SLOs: 99th pctl latency <= 150ms for short-chat responses (<= 256 tokens), p50 ~ 30-50ms.
- Throughput: expected to average 200 RPS for chat during peak campaign windows (9am	611am PT), sustained for ~6 weeks; embedding batch jobs ~20k rows nightly.
- Concurrency: ~50 concurrent active chat sessions (each may open 1	3 parallel requests while rendering), plus connection pooling from our front-end (we typically reuse ~10 persistent connections per instance).
- Streaming: yes 	6 we rely on partial tokens for early render; streaming support and head-of-line fairness are important.

Outstanding from our side: can you confirm Redwood's rate limits/quota options (per-account quotas, per-route concurrency limits), and whether short-term quota bumps are available for the pilot? Also want a quick note on recommended connection pool settings and whether you support keep-alive and multiplexing (HTTP/2).

I'm looping in procurement (procurement@acme.com) 	6 if we decide to move forward we may need formal pricing and a SOW.

Thanks,
Alex
Director of Product 	6 Acme Bot

Hey Alex 	6 great to meet you and thanks for the clear recap. Below are clarifications and immediate next steps. I quoted a few lines from your email inline.

> Target SLOs: 99th pctl latency <= 150ms for short-chat responses (<= 256 tokens)
We can support that target on our Dedicated tiers for models in the 7B	13B family with optimized kernels and prefix caching. For Hosted API, typical customers hit ~150	250ms 99p for similar workloads; to reliably hit 150ms 99p we recommend Dedicated or a hosted + reserved concurrency guarantee.

> Throughput: expected to average 200 RPS for chat during peak
200 RPS sustained is feasible but depends on average prompt/response token lengths and batching behavior. Two options:
- Dedicated GPU pool (recommended): reserved throughput with explicit concurrency capacity and autoscaling policies.
- Hosted with quota + temporary bump: we can provision a pilot quota increase but it's rate-limited by our shared cluster policies.

> Concurrency: ~50 concurrent active chat sessions (1	3 parallel requests each)
We define concurrency in the platform as active inference tokens/streams per model worker + API-level concurrent request slots. For your pattern (~50 users * 2 parallel requests = ~100 concurrent requests), we'd map that to an initial concurrency quota of ~120 to allow headroom.

> Streaming: yes 	6 partial tokens for early render
We support streaming over HTTP/2 and WebSocket. Keep-alive/multiplexing: our hosted endpoints use HTTP/2 for streaming and connection reuse; for Dedicated we recommend HTTP/2 + a pool of persistent connections (8	12 per instance) depending on client concurrency.

Next steps I propose:
1) Run a 2-week pilot with a temporary quota bump to match estimated peak (200 RPS / concurrency 120).
2) Rishi (cc'd) will prepare a preliminary quote for Dedicated vs Hosted pilot and include uplift pricing for a temporary quota bump.
3) We'll need a simple traffic sample from your side (JSONL of ~1k representative requests covering short chat + stream flag + embedding batch) so our infra team can validate batching and kernel selection.

Can you send the traffic sample and confirm procurement contact? I'll attach a pilot quote and the standard pilot SOW.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- Typical tokens: prompt ~60 tokens, response ~120 tokens average for chat; embedding text length ~250 tokens.
- Peak concurrency math: 50 active sessions * avg 2 parallel = 100 active requests. Allowing for retries and spikes we'd like 150 concurrent slots.
- Streaming: critical for perceived latency; we expect clients to open persistent HTTP/2 streams.

Procurement contact is procurement@acme.com (Samantha Lee is the procurement lead). Attached a small traffic sample and expected daily embedding batch sizes.

Alex 	6 all good, thanks for the sample. Quick summary & proposal so procurement has what they need:

- Temporary hosted quota bump: yes 	6 we can grant a time-limited increase to support 200 RPS and 150 concurrent request slots for a 2-week pilot. Requirements: signed pilot MSA (standard terms) and a valid payment method on file.
- Cost delta: approx +60% over baseline hosted list rates for the two-week bump (due to dedicated burst capacity). Exact figure in the attached pilot quote.
- Dedicated pilot: alternative is a 1-month Dedicated reservation sized to your concurrency target (recommended if you plan to run repeated campaigns). Includes SLA for latency and dedicated throughput; pricing included in attached quote.
- Connection pool guidance: start with 10 persistent HTTP/2 connections per application instance, increase if you observe head-of-line queuing; enable keep-alive and avoid short lived connections.
- Observability: we'll provide per-route token/latency breakdown, 99p latency heatmaps, and a sample tracing hook so you can correlate frontend request ids to Redwood inference traces.

Next steps:
1) I'll upload the pilot quote and pilot SOW to the HubSpot deal and share the DocuSign link for the pilot MSA.
2) If procurement approves hosted pilot, we'll provision the quota bump and run a smoke test with your traffic sample (we'll coordinate a 30-min window).

Looping procurement 	6 Samantha, happy to jump on a 15-min call to review the quote and timeline.
